_comment: UPRISING — the facts the announcement is built from.
Single source of truth for everything the posts advertise, the same way
blackout-season.json is for Vol.8. The FORMAT numbers are NOT in here: they
are read out of uprising-engine.js by ops/uprising-facts.mjs, so a post can
never advertise a court count, a round count or a points table that the app
contradicts. Only the things the engine cannot know — when, how much, what
you win — live here.
DATE. The series runs EVERY SATURDAY, not monthly as the first
announcement said. `date` is always the NEXT one; roll it forward by
seven after each night and every card, caption, the link preview and the
landing panel re-render, including the date block, which reads TOMORROW
or TONIGHT while that is true and the date otherwise.
PRIZES. ONE prize for the first night: the champion takes a 15 OMR voucher
and nothing else is advertised (see secondPrize below). championPrizeKind
prints 'voucher' under the figure on every card and inside the sentence in
every message — 'champion takes 15 OMR' reads as cash, and somebody turning
up expecting notes would have been misled by our own poster.
The second prize is kept here, switched off: THE CLIMB — most points above
your own average — takes a free entry rather than cash, which costs 7 OMR
of foregone entry instead of 15 in vouchers and brings the winner back next
month. Measured over 200 simulated seasons, a scratch prize alone sends 70%
of nights to the top three players and the handicap 21%, so it is worth
turning back on once there is history to compute it from.
CADENCE LINE. `cadenceLine` is the only place the rhythm is written. It
was "One Saturday a month" while the series was monthly, and it was
TYPED into landing/index.html as a heading as well, which is how a page
ends up contradicting its own JSON. It is spliced from here now, between
UP:CADENCE markers, the same way the date and the figures are.
name: UPRISING
climbPrize: A free entry to the next UPRISING
_secondPrize: FALSE = one prize only. The champion takes the voucher and nothing else
is advertised. Set by the owner for the first night: a second prize that
has to be explained is a second thing that can go wrong on a night nobody
has played before, and the entry fee is the only other number on the card.
The engine still computes upPrizes() — the stress harness asserts on it —
but nothing in the app or the posts reads it while this is false. Set it
true (and firstNight false, once there is history) to put THE CLIMB back,
and every card and caption re-renders with the second block.
_firstNight: FALSE since the first night was played on 10 Oct 2026. While it was true
the posts called the advertised date "the first one", and THE CLIMB was
replaced by the STRONGEST FINISH, because on night one nobody has an
average: every baseline falls back to the field average, the same number
for everyone, so the rule collapses into "most points" and awards the
champion both prizes. Measured: 2000 of 2000 simulated first nights.
With history behind it THE CLIMB is computable again — though nothing
renders it while secondPrize is false.
_courts: How many courts the club actually has. NOT a rule of the format — the
ladder, the points table and the climb all live in uprising-engine.js.
This is the one number the engine cannot know, and everything downstream
reads it through ops/uprising-facts.mjs: the cards, the captions, the
sign-up list, the link preview and the app's own home page and setup
Four is the norm, and what UPRISING is built around. The first night ran
on THREE under a `courtsOverride` key — a one-off that expired by itself
when the date rolled forward. It has been removed now the night is
played; add it back the same way if a future night is short of a court:
It applies only while its date still equals `date` above, so rolling the
date forward undoes it without anybody having to remember this exists.
It changes more than the ladder's height: with 16 on 3 courts, 4 rest
every round, which means fewer matches each and NO double final — the
player resting the last round could not win it, so the engine switches
the doubling off and every line advertising it disappears with it.
